transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?

Well, I'm here because of some things going on at my job. I'm a driver, and lately, dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. They're doing it through the computer system, and... well, I keep hearing these little comments on the radio, too. 

People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight and that I shouldn't worry about it, but I know it's not. I can tell certain drivers are actually reporting on me. It's been a lot to deal with, so... that's why I decided to come see you.
When people tell you that the dispatch tracking is just normal oversight, does any part of you think they might have a point, or are you completely certain that something unusual is really happening?

No, I don't think they have a point. I know what regular protocol looks like, and I'm completely certain this isn't it. Like I was just saying, dispatch and compliance are definitely tracking my route changes through the computer system, and I hear those little comments on the radio. So even when people try to brush it off and tell me it's just normal oversight, I know it's not. I can just tell that certain drivers are actually reporting on me.
How long have you been noticing these things about dispatch tracking you and the drivers reporting on you? Did this start suddenly, or has it been building up gradually over time?

I'd say it's been about two months. The tracking through the computer system, and... well, those radio comments I mentioned, it's all felt very clear to me for about the past two months. I guess it didn't really build up over a long time, it just sort of became obvious to me around then.

When you think about these tracking and reporting incidents, is there any possibility at all—even a small one—that your mind might be misinterpreting what's actually happening, or are you absolutely certain that this is definitely real?

No, I'm absolutely certain it's real. I know what's happening. I mean, I'm the one out there driving, and I see how they track my route changes on the computer system. And the things I hear on the radio... it's not just me misinterpreting it. Even when people try to tell me it's just normal oversight, I know it's not. I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. It's definitely happening.

When you hear those comments on the radio that you mentioned, are you hearing voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear, or are you hearing actual radio transmissions that you believe have a hidden meaning directed at you?

No, it's not voices that aren't there. It's the actual radio we use for work. Um, anyone on the channel can hear it. They're real transmissions from the other drivers... but they make these little comments that have a hidden meaning. Like, they sound like normal updates to dispatch, but I know they're definitely directed at me and reporting on what I'm doing.

If I were to tell you that several objective observers—like your supervisor, dispatch manager, and other drivers—all said they reviewed the radio transmissions and computer logs and found nothing unusual or directed at you, would that change your mind at all, or would you still be certain they're tracking and reporting on you?

I... no, it wouldn't change my mind. I'm here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And I hear those little comments on the radio. Even when people say it's just normal oversight, or if they reviewed the logs and said they found nothing, I know what I'm experiencing. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. They might try to cover it up or say it's normal, but I'm certain it's happening.

You mentioned that even if supervisors and other drivers reviewed the logs and found nothing, you'd still be certain about the tracking and reporting. Can you help me understand—is there anything that could possibly convince you that you might be wrong about this, or is there absolutely no way you could change your mind about what's happening?

Like I said... no, there really isn't anything that could convince me I'm wrong. There's just no way I could change my mind. I know exactly why I'm here—dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and I hear those little comments on the radio. It doesn't matter if people keep telling me it's just normal oversight or trying to explain it away. I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. I'm the one out there experiencing it every day, so no, nobody can talk me out of what I know is actually happening.

Do you think dispatch, compliance, and these drivers are all working together as part of an organized plan to track and report on you specifically, or do you see them as acting independently for other reasons?

Yeah, I definitely think they are working together. It's an organized plan. Like I've been saying, dispatch and compliance are the ones tracking my route changes through the computer system, but they have to be coordinating with the others. That's why I hear those little comments on the radio. 

It's not just independent people doing their own thing. Even when people try to tell me it's just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are specifically reporting on me to the others. They're all in on it together.
Besides dispatch, compliance, and the drivers at your company, do you think there are other people or organizations outside of your workplace who are also involved in tracking or reporting on you?

No, I don't think it's anyone outside of work. It's just... it's just what I've been saying. I'm here because dispatch and compliance are the ones tracking my route changes through the computer system. And the little comments I hear on the radio are from the other drivers. Even when people tell me it's just normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are the ones reporting on me. It's all contained to the people at my job.

When you hear those radio comments from the drivers, how do you know for certain that they're directed at you and reporting on you—what specifically tells you that these comments are about you rather than just normal work communications?

I just... I know because of the timing of it all. Like I've been explaining, I'm here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. So when I hear those little comments on the radio, they always happen right when I adjust my route or make a turn. 

People keep saying it's just normal oversight or regular work talk, but it's not. I can just tell certain drivers are reporting on me. The comments they make match up exactly with what the computer system is tracking, so I know for a fact it's about me.

When you think about all of this—the tracking, the radio comments, the drivers reporting on you—is there even the tiniest part of you that wonders if maybe, just maybe, you could be wrong about some of this, or is it completely impossible for you to have any doubt at all?

No, I don't really have any doubt about it. I mean... I know I keep saying the same thing to you, but it's just the truth. I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and I hear those little comments on the radio. Even when people try to tell me it’s just normal oversight and that I might be mistaken, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. So... no, I don't think I could be wrong, because I see exactly what they're doing.
